caption: Closed-loop sepsis co-simulation at severity 3 over 2 h (120 s/tick). ONE process-bigraph composite couples the Tellurium sepsis physiology engine to an antibiotic-PK controller process; they exchange state every tick (controller reads the pathogen, integrates a one-compartment PK, writes the drug-killed pathogen back via the engine's parameters_in port). Untreated (controller inert) is the matched control. The loop clears bacteremia — the driver of septic collapse — while the untreated arm's pathogen climbs. The downstream clinical endpoint (MAP < 65 mmHg at ~54 h, tissue integrity 0.24 at 72 h; studies 03/05) is a 2–3 day process not reached at this horizon; this figure shows the controlled variable and the controller's live PK, i.e. the loop removing the cause. The treated arm's sawtooth is the per-tick coupling made visible: the pathogen regrows within each physiology step and the controller knocks it back down at every tick. (At this horizon the untreated arm's tissue integrity has only just begun to fall, ~0.983 vs 1.000 treated — the early edge of the collapse.)
